structure_of_native_mechanism: NetherPortalBlock.entityInside first checks canChangeDimensions (neither vehicle nor passenger) then marks the portal. Server handling refers to corresponding Overworld/Nether ServerLevel, enabled Nether, portal wait/cooldown and Forge travel-event acceptance. Vanilla PortalForcer uses the interface default reposition callback and level exit resolution. A missing or vetoed destination stops before tracked cross-level admission.

With valid PortalInfo, the default callback constructs the same type at destination, saves old data without the type id, removes Dimension and loads it into the fresh object. Base save/load includes UUID and persistent properties. Item serialization carries stack, Health, Age, PickupDelay, Lifespan, Thrower and Owner when present. Identity UUID survives the default path even when Java instance and level change; X/Y/Z and velocity are set by the portal instead.

ServerLevel.addDuringTeleport forwards to addEntity but returns void; addEntity itself delegates to the destination entity manager. Forge posts EntityJoinLevelEvent before UUID uniqueness and section storage. Creation, join-listener observation and return object are distinct from actual destination admission. In the default callback parent, source removeAfterChangingDimensions uses CHANGED_DIMENSION after placeEntity without checking an admission outcome. CHANGED_DIMENSION is a source removal reason, not a proof of arrival.

ItemEntity.changeDimension checks the returned value and immediately asks a destination ItemEntity to merge with neighbors. Merge has compatibility filters and can change which UUID retains the resources. A successfully transferred unmerged item can still be tracked by original UUID in the destination; same item name or target-world stack alone does not establish identity. This is world transfer, distinct from inventory insertion.

If using this mechanism as comparison in a later authorized diagnostic, bind source ServerLevel and object, same UUID, actual native travel/placement result, destination candidate object, real admission plus same-object readback (or immediate validated call), source removal reason, actual later merge participants, and eventual player/handler destination. Keep a separately directed checkout for slot delta and native acquisition. A same-world observer null, event, copied stack or returned candidate object cannot supply missing edges.

dedup.difference: Existing dimensional exposure changes an actor into another species and has a different conversion invariant. This candidate retains the ItemEntity UUID and state while constructing a new object across two ServerLevels, with an immediate target-world merge opportunity.

An accepted projectile landing may create a separate encounter at the origin. That does not transplant an already-existing loose item identity between per-dimension registries, or check its destination after a merge.

An Allay picks an existing loose item then delivers payload through custody and a separate throw. This path serializes the loose item as a world actor and can preserve its UUID in transit, with no NPC acquisition.

dedup_boundary: One proposed corpus item for the combined identity restoration/admission/merge order. Portal construction, item merge, general pickup, Forge event hooks and supporting methods grant zero on their own; earlier merge and backpack receipts retained.
relation_to_oil: A genuine cross-dimension transfer is a distinct possibility for a general loose item. No travel evidence for the selected archived oil or any other lantern oil was added. A custom mod teleporter is not claimed to share default identity/admission semantics.
